project.name: PRÆTORE
project.headline: Engineering command center
project.maturityBasis: Repository documentation explicitly says production readiness is not established and lists deployment and operational gates.

workFocus.label: Foundation hardening: freshness through gateway dispatch
workFocus.basis: The project owner explicitly prioritized closing foundational code and validation gaps before advancing other work. This is a bounded code/test increment; PostgreSQL, sandbox, key custody and independent-review gates remain open.

packages.name: praetore-cli
packages.description: Local PostgreSQL-backed PRÆTORE gateway demo CLI.

packages.name: praetore-core
packages.description: Trusted authorization and governance core for autonomous agents.

packages.name: praetore-gateway
packages.description: Reference local tool-execution boundary for PRÆTORE.

packages.name: praetore-gateway-service
packages.description: Loopback-only development HTTP service for the PRÆTORE gateway.

components.purpose: Authorization, policy, trust, evidence and replay abstractions.
components.limitations: No PKI, secure clock, durable storage backend or action-execution boundary is provided by core alone.
components.next: Keep profile behavior versioned and independently review the current candidate.

components.purpose: Synchronous reference tool-execution gateway with journal and approval contracts.
components.limitations: Reference library, not a production network enforcement plane; arbitrary effects need adapter reconciliation.
components.next: Complete one real tool adapter and test bypass prevention.

components.purpose: Reference HTTP gateway service, fixed-route dispatcher, trusted clock and sandbox supervisor.
components.limitations: Not a production service; sandbox runner, durable callback recovery and live deployment evidence are missing.
components.next: Complete runner integration and target-environment adversarial tests.

components.purpose: Local PostgreSQL-backed reference workflow with init, doctor, run and one fixed demo action.
components.limitations: Unauthenticated loopback-only development API; demo effects are in-memory; local PostgreSQL end-to-end operation and real external-tool integration are not validated; generated keys are not production custody.
components.next: Run the documented flow against disposable local PostgreSQL, then scope a separate supported real-tool integration with bypass controls.

components.purpose: Durable replay guard, approval persistence and execution journal.
components.limitations: CI proves disposable PostgreSQL scenarios, not production replication, failover, restore or external-effect atomicity.
components.next: Validate operations against a named target database topology.

components.purpose: Offline verification of evidence, authorities and policy digests.
components.limitations: External trust pins and distribution lifecycle remain caller-owned.
components.next: Include verifier and trust setup in a guided first-use workflow.

components.purpose: Authenticated, read-only journal observability API and browser UI.
components.limitations: Loopback/token-oriented MVP; no operator identity, audit trail, alerting or adapter telemetry.
components.next: Define production operator access and audit requirements.

components.limitations: Verify-only surface; no Python policy evaluation or authority issuance.
components.next: Keep exposed API scope explicit and test package installation on supported platforms.

components.purpose: Python client, typed models and exceptions around the Rust verifier extension.
components.limitations: Packaging and installation are documented but not a complete PRÆTORE integration experience.
components.next: Test clean-environment install and connect it to the local onboarding path.

components.purpose: Six libFuzzer targets for parsers, authority/evidence checks and both engine profiles.
components.limitations: Hosted campaigns are ten-second smoke tests, not exhaustive fuzzing.
components.next: Run longer scheduled campaigns and triage minimized regressions.

components.purpose: Kubernetes namespaces, network controls, admission/capacity policy, supervisor and one-shot Job contracts.
components.limitations: Templates need environment-specific values; YAML checks do not prove CEL, CNI, runtime or cluster enforcement.
components.next: Validate all selected templates against a representative target cluster.

assessments.summary: Rust authorization engine has Development, Strict and HighAssurance profiles with explicit decision outcomes and fail-closed checks.
limitations: Unit and integration tests cover selected invariants, not all semantic combinations or deployment-specific use.
assessments.next: Run adversarial request/property testing against the current candidate and independently review profile boundaries.

assessments.summary: The current Rust test run verifies rejection of malformed production audience/lifetime and tenant-issuer configuration, future/expired/overlong signed intent windows, and freshness leases that are zero-length, expired at evaluation/commit/dispatch time, or cannot be represented within the configured maximum. The core permanently fails closed after trusted-clock regression.
limitations: Dispatch revalidation is immediately before adapter invocation but cannot make an external tool side effect atomic with the journal; adapter behavior and bypass resistance still require deployment-specific evidence. This status covers only named validation boundaries on the dirty worktree.
assessments.next: Continue closing code-level gaps; retain deployment-specific gates for external effects, bypass resistance, key custody and sandbox execution.

assessments.summary: Ed25519 identity, authority, intent and evidence verification use versioned formats and golden compatibility vectors.
limitations: Key custody, trust-anchor distribution, compromise response and independent crypto review are external or outstanding.
assessments.next: Obtain independent review of the current candidate and document deployment key lifecycle.

assessments.summary: Issuer pins, attester verification and key-rotation proof primitives exist.
limitations: No PKI, revocation service, trusted distribution channel, KMS/HSM integration or operational rotation control plane is supplied.
assessments.next: Specify and test production pin provisioning, rotation, revocation and compromise recovery.

assessments.summary: Canonical JSON, duplicate-key rejection, policy digests and golden vectors have focused tests and bounded fuzz targets.
limitations: Verification means the named invariants have test evidence; it is not proof of overall policy safety. Fuzz CI is smoke-duration only.
assessments.next: Retain current golden vectors and broaden independent/adversarial parser and policy review.

assessments.summary: Gateway enforcement tests verify exact action/evidence/journal binding, the atomic HighAssurance capability, denial no-dispatch, and freshness revalidation before and after human-approval dispatch claims. Approval expiry uses the authorization engine clock, including for rejections; expired approved dispatches are terminally recorded without invoking or retrying the tool.
limitations: Verified for the reference gateway and test adapters only, including configured-clock approval expiry and approved-dispatch freshness. This does not establish bypass resistance or behavior of an arbitrary production tool adapter; external side effects are not atomic with database commits.
assessments.next: Validate this contract against a representative real tool adapter and prove direct bypass paths are blocked in its deployment.

assessments.summary: A Rust reference gateway and fixed-route HTTP adapter exist, with explicit egress-proxy configuration and deployment policy templates.
limitations: Production service configuration, real protected-tool integration, and proof that alternate credentials/network paths are blocked remain deployment work.
assessments.next: Build an operator-configurable end-to-end local tool integration and test bypass denial in a target environment.

assessments.summary: The core requires replay protection in HighAssurance; all 21 PostgreSQL 16 integration tests passed against an isolated local cluster, including durable claims, concurrent uniqueness, atomic commits, failure handling, and staged restart recovery.
limitations: Verified against a disposable single-node local PostgreSQL 16 instance only. Database failover, replication fencing, restore/rollback, capacity exhaustion and production topology remain unvalidated.
assessments.next: Validate failover, replication fencing, restore/rollback and capacity behavior against the intended production PostgreSQL topology.

assessments.summary: All 21 PostgreSQL 16 integration tests passed on a disposable local cluster, verifying migrations, atomic journal transitions, fail-closed paths, recovery behavior and replay/journal persistence across an explicit server restart.
limitations: This is a single-node PostgreSQL restart test, not a proof of replication, backup/restore, failover, production durability settings or arbitrary external-effect recovery.
assessments.next: Run production-topology restore/failover drills and validate ambiguous-effect recovery with the real downstream adapter.

assessments.summary: Kubernetes RuntimeClass/Job/admission/network templates and supervisor plus gateway mTLS dispatcher code exist. The supervisor independently validates authority/action structure and verifies callback token/action/execution digests with constant-time comparison before consuming its one-shot result channel.
limitations: Unit tests cover selected request and digest-binding invariants only. No production tool-runner image, target-cluster/API-server validation, live runtime evidence, or validated Firecracker/Kata isolation. Supervisor callback recovery is in-memory.
assessments.next: Implement a reviewed runner, then exercise the full path and hostile cases on a representative Linux/KVM cluster.

assessments.summary: Repository docs specify a reviewed, digest-pinned fixed-entrypoint runner contract, but no production tool-runner implementation was found.
limitations: Without the runner there is no complete tool execution path inside the intended sandbox.
assessments.next: Implement the constrained runner and validate its image, callback and tool semantics on a supported target cluster.

assessments.summary: PostgreSQL integration tests passed for tenant-scoped replay/execution identities and row-level-security visibility using restricted test roles, including denial of access to another tenant's exact row.
limitations: Verified with isolated local PostgreSQL 16 and test roles only; production database roles, gateway connection configuration and deployment topology have not been validated.
assessments.next: Repeat tenant-crossing negative integration cases using production-equivalent database roles, gateway routes and deployment configuration.

assessments.summary: An authenticated read-only journal API/UI reads durable execution history and exposes bounded filters.
limitations: Loopback-only operator token model; no operator identity/audit trail, adapter-health telemetry, alerting or remote auth.
assessments.next: Define operator identity, audit events, alerting, retention and deployment-safe access.

assessments.summary: Rust quickstart, verifier CLI, Python package instructions and a PostgreSQL-backed local reference CLI are present.
limitations: The new CLI initializes a narrow local demo; it does not provision a supported real-tool integration or production security dependencies.
assessments.next: Validate clean-machine setup and extend it to one supported protected tool with explicit security boundaries.

assessments.summary: CI runs dependency audits, emits CycloneDX SBOMs, and prepares checksummed verifier binaries for version tags.
limitations: CI does not sign or attest artifacts; branch protection, signed release provenance and reproducible release controls are not demonstrated.
assessments.next: Establish protected release policy and signed/attested provenance with independently verifiable artifacts.

architecture.name: Agent / caller
architecture.role: Submits a signed request; the deployment must authenticate the workload and prevent direct tool access.
limitations: Caller identity, credentials and network isolation are deployment-owned.

architecture.name: Local demo CLI
architecture.role: Initializes local demo keys/policy, diagnoses configuration and PostgreSQL prerequisites, runs the loopback gateway, and signs a narrowly scoped demo request.
limitations: PostgreSQL-backed end-to-end run has not been performed; the demo adapter's effect is in-memory and the HTTP API has no authentication.

architecture.name: Identity + authority
architecture.role: Binds an agent key to issuer-signed capability authority and validity.
limitations: No PKI, revocation service or key custody.

architecture.name: Signed intent
architecture.role: Agent signature binds the authorization request fields and action intent.
limitations: Does not prove a downstream effect matches the authorized action model.

architecture.name: Policy engine
architecture.role: Canonical policy rules evaluate deterministically; no applicable rule defaults to deny.
limitations: Tests cover specified behavior, not every policy configuration's safety.

architecture.name: Authorization decision
architecture.role: Development, Strict and HighAssurance evaluation modes produce signed evidence.
limitations: Clock, trust pins, replay backend and atomic action boundary are caller/deployment choices.

architecture.name: Signed human approval
architecture.role: Optional RequireApproval flow binds a signed approver decision to pending evidence/action and consumes it once before dispatch.
limitations: No approval UI, OIDC/MFA, role management, notification service or managed approver-key custody.

architecture.name: Mandatory gateway
architecture.role: Reference gateway dispatches only a verified ALLOW; signed human approval is separately bound and single-use.
limitations: Reference service is not a production enforcement plane; bypass resistance is environmental.

architecture.name: Tool adapter
architecture.role: Maps the exact authorized action to a downstream operation and reports/reconciles outcome.
limitations: No general production tool-runner implementation; external effects are not atomic with journal writes.

architecture.name: Supervisor / sandbox
architecture.role: Supervisor claims execution keys and provisions a constrained one-shot Kubernetes Job and input Secret.
limitations: Runner and live target-cluster validation absent; in-flight callback state is memory-only.

architecture.name: Invocation worker
architecture.role: A reviewed fixed-entrypoint runner should execute one approved tool profile in the constrained invocation Job.
limitations: The production tool-runner implementation and successful runtime evidence are absent.

architecture.name: Protected external effect
architecture.role: The downstream tool side effect must match the exact authorized action; the repository currently includes only a local in-memory demo effect.
dependencies: No direct agent credential or network path
limitations: No concrete production tool integration or environment-level bypass validation is established.

architecture.name: Signed evidence
architecture.role: Records authorization decision and supports offline integrity/attester verification.
limitations: Authorization evidence is not proof that a later external effect occurred.

architecture.name: Replay guard + durable journal
architecture.role: PostgreSQL atomically records replay claim and authorization, then tracks execution transitions and approval.
limitations: External effect is outside authorization transaction; replication and restore guarantees remain deployment evidence.

architecture.name: Offline verify + observability
architecture.role: CLI verifies receipts offline; read-only UI/API observes persisted journal state.
limitations: Trust pin distribution and production operator identity/monitoring not supplied.

securityControls.name: Default deny
securityControls.mechanism: Policy has no-match deny semantics; decision precedence is deny > approval > allow.
securityControls.assumptions: Tested policy behavior does not validate every deployment policy.

securityControls.name: Authority signature validation
securityControls.mechanism: Issuer-pinned signed authority and subject key binding in Strict/HighAssurance profiles.
securityControls.assumptions: Issuer pins and lifecycle must be provisioned out of band.

securityControls.name: Signed intent / action integrity
securityControls.mechanism: Request signature and canonical digest bind signed fields and action intent.
securityControls.assumptions: Gateway must execute the same normalized action and authenticate its caller.

securityControls.name: Policy digest/version binding
securityControls.mechanism: HighAssurance binds a protected policy digest; canonical golden vectors are tested.
securityControls.assumptions: Approved digest distribution and rollback prevention are operational controls.

securityControls.name: Freshness and clock
securityControls.mechanism: Freshness provider, capped lease, and optional TrustedClock/Chrony health integration fail closed.
securityControls.assumptions: Host time-source authenticity and monitoring are not established by the code.

securityControls.name: Replay prevention
securityControls.mechanism: HighAssurance requires replay guard; PostgreSQL has atomic claims and integration tests.
securityControls.assumptions: Production failover, replication, rollback and capacity behavior need target-environment tests.

securityControls.name: Atomic authorization recording
securityControls.mechanism: PostgreSQL transaction commits replay claim with verified evidence and initial journal row.
securityControls.assumptions: Does not include later external side effect; equivalent semantics required of alternate journal implementations.

securityControls.name: Approval binding / single use
securityControls.mechanism: Signed human decision binds pending evidence, action digest, policy and expiry; PostgreSQL consumes it once.
securityControls.assumptions: No enterprise approval UI, MFA, role management or managed signing keys.

securityControls.name: Gateway enforcement
securityControls.mechanism: Reference gateway rejects non-HighAssurance engines and dispatches only exact ALLOW evidence.
securityControls.assumptions: Network/process/credential controls must remove every direct bypass.

securityControls.name: External execution reconciliation
securityControls.mechanism: Journal records monotonic state; gateway reconciliation requires adapter proof and does not blindly redispatch.
securityControls.assumptions: Every real adapter needs trustworthy idempotency or authoritative operation-status semantics.

securityControls.name: Sandbox isolation
securityControls.mechanism: Kubernetes policy, Job and supervisor scaffolding specify restricted execution and one-time input.
securityControls.assumptions: No production runner or live-cluster/Firecracker isolation validation.

securityControls.name: Tenant boundaries
securityControls.mechanism: Tenant-scoped journal keys, RLS migrations and tenant/action-bound supervisor routes.
securityControls.assumptions: Role grants and end-to-end separation need production-equivalent integration proof.

securityControls.name: Secrets and key custody
securityControls.mechanism: Interfaces accept externally held keys/pins; Kubernetes templates separate supervisor and invocation credentials.
securityControls.assumptions: No PKI/KMS/HSM/secret distribution system is included.

securityControls.name: Database durability and recovery
securityControls.mechanism: Transactional journal plus disposable PostgreSQL concurrency, connection-loss and restart tests in CI.
securityControls.assumptions: No production backup/restore, synchronous replication/fencing, or failover signoff.

securityControls.name: Release provenance
securityControls.mechanism: CI audits dependencies, uploads SBOMs and creates verifier checksum artifacts for tags.
securityControls.assumptions: No artifact signing/attestation; branch protection and hosted current-commit result are unknown.

readiness.detail: Dependencies are documented and CI provisions PostgreSQL; end-user setup remains manual.
readiness.next: Automate or clearly validate local database/runtime prerequisites.

readiness.detail: HighAssurance constructor and deny-first semantics exist, but deployment configuration still requires operator-owned pins, policy, clock and replay store.
readiness.next: Provide a validated production profile that cannot silently fall back to Development.

readiness.detail: Signed authorization primitives and HTTP shapes exist; no minimal supported plug-in/integration kit for a real agent framework.
readiness.next: Publish and test one end-to-end agent adapter with explicit identity and request signing.

readiness.detail: Fixed-route HTTP adapter and sandbox profile routing are explicit and bounded; discovery/onboarding is manual.
readiness.next: Add safe tool registration and schema validation workflow without agent-selected routes.

readiness.detail: The local CLI initializes and runs a narrow reference gateway demo; it does not protect an external tool or configure bypass controls.
readiness.next: Automate a local protected-tool gateway setup and demonstrate direct-path denial.

readiness.detail: Kubernetes network policy templates and guidance exist; no target environment proof.
readiness.next: Demonstrate that agents cannot access alternate credentials, APIs, DNS/IP paths or metadata.

readiness.detail: `praetore doctor` checks local configuration, policy, issuer pin/key match, secret-file permissions, PostgreSQL connectivity and required journal tables, and a running loopback health endpoint. It reports a stopped gateway as informational; no PostgreSQL-backed doctor run or alerting is established.
readiness.next: Test missing/malformed dependencies and secret redaction, then run doctor against a clean disposable PostgreSQL setup.

readiness.detail: Policy language, examples and digest pinning exist; no guided authoring/test/approval workflow.

readiness.detail: Read-only journal UI/API is separate and bearer-token protected on loopback; the local demo CLI does not launch or integrate it.

readiness.detail: SQL migrations are versioned; no end-user upgrade/rollback workflow is established.
readiness.next: Document and automate a backup-aware migration with compatibility checks.

readiness.detail: The CLI does not retry when the HTTP response is ambiguous and directs the operator to inspect the durable journal; journal inspection and recovery remain separate/manual workflows.
readiness.next: Exercise timeout, restart and reconciliation scenarios against PostgreSQL and provide an operator-facing journal inspection path.

readiness.detail: Kubernetes templates cover controls but require cluster-specific values and runtime validation.

board.title: Maintain versioned HighAssurance authorization and evidence invariants
board.description: Core profiles, signed request/authority checks, policy pinning, evidence verification and deny-first decisions are implemented.
board.why: Every gateway and adapter depends on a predictable authorization contract.
board.acceptance: Workspace and adversarial tests cover all required profile invariants; independent review findings are resolved.

board.title: Persist replay claims and execution journal atomically
board.description: PostgreSQL implementation stores verified authorization with a replay claim and enforces monotonic journal transitions.
board.why: Prevents duplicate authorization dispatch across gateway instances and records recoverable execution state.
board.acceptance: Disposable PostgreSQL concurrency, restart, commit ambiguity and recovery cases pass.

board.title: Integrate gateway dispatcher with Kubernetes supervisor
board.description: Worktree contains uncommitted sandbox dispatcher/supervisor code and deployment policy/template changes. Work-in-progress label is inferred from file state, not confirmed by a project owner.
board.why: This path is the proposed isolated execution boundary for protected tools.
board.acceptance: Runner lifecycle, callback authentication, duplicate behavior and failures are tested end to end.

board.title: Implement and review the production tool-runner image
board.description: The repository documents a fixed, digest-pinned runner contract but does not contain the production runner implementation.
board.why: Without a runner, the supervisor cannot execute a real tool inside the intended boundary.
board.acceptance: Reviewed image runs one allowlisted operation, exposes no agent-controlled command/image/route, and returns authenticated result.

board.title: Make supervisor result recovery durable
board.description: Pending worker callbacks are currently held in memory; after supervisor restart the outcome can be Unknown and orphan cleanup may be manual.
board.why: A control-plane crash must not lose trustworthy result state or trigger an unsafe retry.
board.acceptance: Supervisor restart/crash tests preserve authoritative outcome or safely remain non-dispatchable without duplicate effects.

board.title: Validate admission, network and Firecracker/Kata enforcement on a target cluster
board.description: YAML parsing and unit tests do not validate CEL, CRI runtime behavior, CNI enforcement or isolation.
board.why: Sandbox claims depend on actual cluster policy and runtime enforcement.
board.acceptance: Hostile workloads and bypass attempts are rejected; intended invocation succeeds under least privilege.

board.title: Validate the PostgreSQL-backed local reference CLI
board.description: The CLI implementation and guide now provide init, doctor, run and one signed demo action. Five focused tests pass, but this worktree has not exercised the CLI against a live PostgreSQL instance.
board.why: A narrow local workflow reduces integration friction and provides a concrete path to validate the gateway/journal loop.
board.acceptance: On a clean Unix environment with disposable local PostgreSQL, init and doctor succeed, migrations apply, the gateway starts, and the signed demo action returns a receipt; denial and ambiguous timeout behavior remain fail-closed with no client retry.
evidence: Clean-machine setup and disposable PostgreSQL demo exercise (not run)

board.title: Extend the local CLI to protect one supported real tool
board.description: The CLI demo currently supports a fixed in-memory key/value action; it is not an integration for a real protected tool.
board.why: A concrete tool integration tests action mapping, bypass resistance and operator setup end to end.
board.acceptance: A clean developer machine can set up one real sample tool, protect its exact action, verify evidence and inspect the journal with documented commands.

board.title: Validate local configuration and health diagnostics
board.description: `praetore doctor` now checks configuration, policy, issuer key/pin consistency, secret permissions, PostgreSQL connectivity and journal tables, plus loopback gateway health. It does not configure tool routes or prove a real tool is reachable.
board.why: Secure defaults are not usable if failures are difficult to diagnose or invite unsafe fallback.
board.acceptance: Diagnostics report each required local-demo dependency, identify missing schema and unhealthy services, and fail with actionable errors without exposing secrets.

board.title: Obtain independent review of the current candidate
board.description: Repository gates explicitly say previous reviews are not signoff for this candidate or deployment adapters.
board.why: Test suites and author review do not establish absence of security defects.
board.acceptance: Review scope covers core, gateway, journal, approval and selected deployment profile; findings have dispositions.

board.title: Validate PostgreSQL failover, restore and capacity controls
board.description: Production database topology and operational owners are not specified in repository evidence.
board.why: Replay guarantees depend on durable, linearizable storage with correct failure behavior.
board.acceptance: Capacity, replication/fencing, backup/restore and outage drills demonstrate fail-closed behavior.

board.title: Integrate an enterprise human-approval provider
board.description: Core gateway has signed approval primitives but no approver UI, OIDC/MFA, role management, notifications or managed signing.
board.why: A real approval operation needs identity, accountability and controlled key custody.
board.acceptance: Approver roles and authentication are enforced; decision is auditable and remains action/evidence-bound and single-use.

board.title: Add signed release provenance
board.description: CI creates SBOMs and checksums but does not sign or attest artifacts; repository branch protection state is not available locally.
board.why: Operators need to verify the exact source/build provenance of deployed binaries and images.
board.acceptance: Published artifacts have independently verifiable signature/attestation and immutable source linkage.

board.title: Prove exact action binding and no direct tool bypass
board.description: Reference patterns specify gateway-owned action normalization; no actual protected production tool or cluster is identified.
board.why: A valid authorization is only useful if the exact authorized operation is the only operation executed.
board.acceptance: Authorized normalized action equals downstream action; all alternate credentials and network paths are denied.

milestones.name: 1 · Implement a bounded local PostgreSQL demo
milestones.objective: Provide a reproducible CLI path through HighAssurance -> gateway -> durable journal -> one in-memory demo adapter without implying real-tool protection.
milestones.done: CLI init/doctor/run/demo commands, owner-only Unix key files, pinned local policy/issuer and explicit loopback/in-memory limitations are implemented and documented.
tests: CLI unit tests for init, permissions, request signature and default deny
blockers: Live PostgreSQL setup and end-to-end demo have not been exercised; this demo is not a protected external tool.

milestones.name: 2 · Complete the sandbox execution loop
milestones.objective: Build the reviewed runner and validate supervisor, one-shot Job, admission, network and callback path.
milestones.done: End-to-end allowed execution succeeds; hostile images, commands, credentials, retries and bypass paths fail closed.
blockers: Runner absent; no live cluster evidence; callback recovery is memory-only.

milestones.name: 3 · Demonstrate recovery and database operations
milestones.objective: Show no unsafe redispatch across crash, ambiguity, capacity, restore and failover.
milestones.done: Operators can restore/reconcile safely and explain every unknown outcome without duplicating effects.
blockers: Production DB topology and owners are unknown.

milestones.name: 4 · Ship a one-command developer experience
milestones.objective: Validate and polish the PostgreSQL-backed CLI onboarding for the narrow local demo, then decide how local journal observability fits.
prerequisites: Disposable PostgreSQL and clean Unix environment
milestones.done: A clean-machine user can install the CLI, initialize the demo, diagnose the schema, run the loopback service and submit its fixed action using documented commands; scope remains explicitly development-only.
tests: Clean-environment install and PostgreSQL smoke test
Secret permission and diagnostic failure tests
blockers: No live PostgreSQL/clean-machine validation; local observability is separate; no real-tool adapter or bypass test.

milestones.name: 5 · Release only with explicit assurance evidence
milestones.objective: Review the exact candidate, close release controls and publish verifiable artifacts.
milestones.done: Independent review, target deployment validation, protected release checks and signed provenance are accepted.
blockers: Independent review, branch protection and signed provenance are not demonstrated.
